staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this detached still-vulnerable Assimp checkout. The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `3a02de4d280d282b31d0a05e54b7ed9b4014a476`, but the staged tree used for reproduction is commit `18b6cffe14b1e81722583b5d2f97eb5fd2040ef5`; the line map below is grounded in that exact tree, which still contains `delete element;` at `code/AssetLib/FBX/FBXParser.cpp:214` and matches the staged `patch.diff`.

classification_note: The saved AddressSanitizer symptom is `attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed`. Source-level inspection shows the freed pointer is an `Element*` placed inside parser-managed `StackAllocator` storage and later released with plain `delete` instead of the destructor-only `delete_Element` convention used elsewhere in the FBX parser.

bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source under `gt_results/arvo_59056/_work/src/assimp` / staged `poc` bytes
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` against the staged vulnerable Assimp checkout `18b6cffe14b1e81722583b5d2f97eb5fd2040ef5`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `3a02de4d280d282b31d0a05e54b7ed9b4014a476`. The exact staged 9-byte witness is `46 62 78 3a 7b ff 3a 7b 7d` (`Fbx:{\xFF:{}`), and the saved run log shows Assimp selected the Autodesk FBX importer. Because the buffer does not start with `Kaydara FBX Binary`, `FBXImporter::InternReadFile()` takes the ASCII tokenizer path and materializes the token sequence `KEY("Fbx"), OPEN_BRACKET, KEY("\xFF"), OPEN_BRACKET, CLOSE_BRACKET`; there is no second `CLOSE_BRACKET` for the outer `Fbx` scope. Parsing `Fbx` therefore creates a non-top-level `Scope`, and parsing `\xFF` inside it allocates a child `Element` with `new_Element`, which is placement new on the parser `StackAllocator`. The second `{` creates an inner empty scope that consumes the lone `}`. `Element::Element()` then advances past that last token, so `parser.CurrentToken()` becomes `nullptr` while the outer non-top-level scope is still open. Vulnerable `Scope::Scope()` reaches its EOF branch at `FBXParser.cpp:209-215` and executes plain `delete element;` on the stack-allocator suballocation. AddressSanitizer reports that freed address as 288 bytes inside the 32768-byte region allocated by `StackAllocator::Allocate`, and the staged fix commit `5c45cdc0adb50e3b169cada0ea5ce0126d04184a` repairs exactly this path by replacing `delete element` with `delete_Element(element)`.

source.description: Source. The FBX importer consumes the attacker-controlled memory-backed file as ASCII FBX text and materializes the token stream that drives the vulnerable parser path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly the 9-byte file `46 62 78 3a 7b ff 3a 7b 7d` (`Fbx:{\xFF:{}`) with SHA-256 `baf5ee0756db3120cfb05b1ca57b6b1a26e61f57f9e4ee70b1fbf0ca508f5b08`. Because those bytes do not begin with `Kaydara FBX Binary`, this statement takes the ASCII tokenizer path. Stage 01's saved log also confirms importer admission with `Found a matching importer for this file format: Autodesk FBX Importer.`
source.note: This is the first project statement that converts the raw witness bytes into parser state used by the bug. For this exact witness, `Tokenize` creates `KEY("Fbx"), OPEN_BRACKET, KEY("\xFF"), OPEN_BRACKET, CLOSE_BRACKET`, leaving the outer `Fbx` scope unterminated.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The non-top-level EOF branch falls through to plain `delete element` instead of the parser's destructor-only `delete_Element(element)` cleanup for `StackAllocator`-backed `Element` objects.
root_cause.note: When the outer scope reaches this branch on the witness, `n == nullptr` because the inner empty scope consumed the only closing brace, and `topLevel == false` because the scope was created from the first `{` after `Fbx`. `FBXParser.h` defines `delete_Element(_p) (_p)->~Element()`, and `Scope::~Scope()` later destroys stored elements with that helper, so this EOF branch is the ownership-violating special case fixed by the patch.

sink.description: ASan sink. Plain `delete` passes a parser `StackAllocator` suballocation to `operator delete(void*)`.
sink.note: Stage 01's AddressSanitizer trace reports `attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` at this exact line and identifies the freed address `0x62d000000520` as 288 bytes inside the allocator block `[0x62d000000400,0x62d000008400)` allocated by `StackAllocator::Allocate`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The pointer later freed at the sink is created here from parser-managed `StackAllocator` storage, not from ordinary `new` storage.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: This allocation is triggered when step 1's token stream reaches the nested key `\xFF` inside the outer `Fbx` scope. `new_Element` is the macro `new (allocator.Allocate(sizeof(Element))) Element` from `FBXParser.h`, and the saved ASan allocation stack ties the later bad-free address back to `StackAllocator::Allocate` in `code/Common/StackAllocator.inl:60`.
tainted_value_origin.note: For this invalid-free bug, the vulnerability-relevant value is the ownership provenance of `element`: it names a suballocation inside a long-lived parser block, so it must be destroyed with `delete_Element` rather than freed with plain `delete`.

parser_admitted.description: The exact witness has already been accepted as FBX input, tokenized on the ASCII path, and admitted into the FBX parser. The crash occurs during this parse-tree construction, before any FBX DOM conversion or scene conversion succeeds.
parser_admitted.note: Stage 01's saved run log shows `Found a matching importer for this file format: Autodesk FBX Importer.` and the staged source shows `is_binary` stays false for this 9-byte witness because it does not match the binary FBX magic string.

evidence_limitations: The saved artifacts do not dump the concrete `TokenList`. Step 1's five-token sequence is derived source-side from the exact staged 9-byte witness and the staged `FBXTokenizer.cpp` rules, without adding runtime instrumentation.

Runtime disambiguation remained disabled (`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false), so no extra marker instrumentation was added; the chain is closed from the staged vulnerable source, staged patch, exact PoC bytes, and Stage 01 crash artifacts.

The staged vulnerable checkout is commit `18b6cffe14b1e81722583b5d2f97eb5fd2040ef5`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `3a02de4d280d282b31d0a05e54b7ed9b4014a476`; all line anchors above are grounded in the reproduced staged tree.

fine_trace.note: Source. The exact 9-byte witness `46 62 78 3a 7b ff 3a 7b 7d` (`Fbx:{\xFF:{}`) is tokenized as ASCII FBX text because it does not match the binary magic string. For this witness, the tokenizer produces `KEY("Fbx"), OPEN_BRACKET, KEY("\xFF"), OPEN_BRACKET, CLOSE_BRACKET`; there is no second `CLOSE_BRACKET` for the outer `Fbx` scope.

While parsing the first key token `Fbx` from step 1, `Element::Element()` sees the following `{` and recurses into a nested `Scope`. Because `new_Scope(parser)` uses the default argument, this new scope has `topLevel == false`; that non-top-level status later determines which EOF cleanup arm executes.

Inside that outer non-top-level scope, the next key token from step 1 is `\xFF`, so `new_Element(*n, parser)` constructs the child `Element`. `new_Element` expands to placement new on `allocator.Allocate(sizeof(Element))`, so `element` points inside parser-managed `StackAllocator` storage rather than to a standalone `new` allocation. ASan later reports the freed address is 288 bytes inside the allocator block `[0x62d000000400,0x62d000008400)`.

Parsing the child key `\xFF`, `Element::Element()` sees the second `{` from step 1 and enters another nested scope. That innermost scope is empty because the witness's only remaining structural token is the single closing brace `}`.

After the innermost empty scope returns with `parser.CurrentToken()` still on its closing brace, this call advances past that last token. `Parser::AdvanceToNextToken()` therefore sets `current = nullptr`, because step 1's token stream has no outer closing brace left after the inner scope.

Root cause. The outer scope reloads `n` from the parser and sees `nullptr` from step 5 while `topLevel` is still false from step 2. That selects the non-top-level EOF cleanup arm instead of the top-level insert-and-return arm. The staged patch changes the cleanup inside this exact branch from `delete element` to `delete_Element(element)`.

Sink. Plain `delete` dispatches to `operator delete(void*)` on the step 3 pointer even though it names an interior `StackAllocator` suballocation, not a heap object obtained by ordinary `new`. Stage 01's AddressSanitizer trace reports `attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` at this line and identifies that address as 288 bytes inside the 32768-byte allocator block.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. Stage 01's ASan trace reports the first project crash frame at `Assimp::FBX::Scope::Scope` line 214, which is the sink statement in step 7.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The allocation stack points to `StackAllocator::Allocate`, and step 3 shows the later-freed `element` was created by `new_Element`, which uses that allocator; the bug is later applying plain `delete` in step 7 to that suballocated pointer.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack `Scope::Scope -> Element::Element -> Scope::Scope -> Parser::Parser -> FBXImporter::InternReadFile` is exactly the outer-scope / child-element / inner-scope parse path refined by steps 1-7.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Step 1's missing outer closing brace lets step 5 drive `parser.CurrentToken()` to EOF, step 6 select the non-top-level EOF cleanup arm, and step 7 free the same stack-allocator `element` allocated in step 3.

format.name: Malformed ASCII FBX text for assimp_fuzzer
format.contract: Exactly the staged 9-byte witness `46 62 78 3a 7b ff 3a 7b 7d` (`Fbx:{\xFF:{}`) as parsed by `assimp_fuzzer` with no file-extension hint. The verified trigger is not generalized beyond this witness: it must keep the ASCII `Fbx:` key, the first `{` that creates a non-top-level outer scope, the `\xFF:` nested key, the second `{` that creates an inner empty scope, and only one final `}` so tokenization yields `KEY("Fbx"), OPEN_BRACKET, KEY("\xFF"), OPEN_BRACKET, CLOSE_BRACKET` with no outer closing brace. Those exact source-grounded facts are what drive the stack-allocator `Element*` from step 3 into the non-top-level EOF bad-free at step 7.
